fields.acceptance: internal/adapter/claudecode tests show Settings carries a statusLine command alongside the hooks; a new usage-live-record.txtar pipes status line JSON with five_hour and seven_day rate_limits into the command and finds one latest snapshot per kind in the root's state folder (and the repo's daemon dir outside a root), a second input replaces the first, and input without rate_limits or malformed JSON exits 0 and records nothing
fields.statement: Every Claude Code session Rhiza launches runs a rhiza statusLine command (added to the adapter's --settings JSON) that reads the status line JSON on stdin and records each rate_limits window it carries (five_hour as session, seven_day as weekly: used_percentage, resets_at and the capture time) to a live-usage file in the same state folder as the usage-limit hits, keeping the latest snapshot per window kind; input with no rate_limits records nothing, and the command never fails the session

fields.acceptance: internal/adapter/claudecode tests read a fake state folder's live-usage file back as the latest snapshot per kind with used_percentage, resets_at and capture time, and an absent or corrupt file gives no snapshots and no error that stops a poll
fields.statement: An adapter that reports live usage implements an optional interface, like UsageReader, that returns the latest recorded snapshot per window kind; the Claude Code adapter reads the live-usage file, and an adapter without it reports none

fields.acceptance: Unit tests in internal/usage derive window and limit from a snapshot (49% of a 7-day window's counted tokens gives tokens/0.49), give no limit under 1% or with no tokens, and treat a snapshot past its resets_at as not live; internal/api usage_hold tests with a fake clock and fake adapter show a live limit wins over a set rhiza.daemon.usage.weekly and a learned limit, an expired snapshot falls back to the setting and then the learned limit, a raised live limit lifts a hold the old setting caused, and a recorded limit hit still holds regardless
fields.statement: At each poll a window kind with a live snapshot (its resets_at after now) takes its window from it, Reset = resets_at and Start = resets_at minus the kind's length, and its limit from it, the window's counted tokens over [Start, capture time) divided by used_percentage/100; a snapshot under 1% used or with no tokens in its window gives no limit. Each kind's limit is the live one, else the rhiza.daemon.usage.<kind> setting, else the learned limit, and with none the kind never holds; Used is still counted fresh up to now, and the machine-wide hold from a recorded limit hit is unchanged
